rows.listen_label: King Institute (Stanford) recording – Pasadena, 28 Feb 1960 delivery
rows.evidence: No recording of the 24 Jan 1954 Dexter trial sermon is online, so this links a later delivery: the King Institute mp3 (audio/mpeg, about 60 min) is named after OKRA record 600228-001, titled "The Three Dimensions of a Complete Life," Sermon delivered at Friendship Baptist Church (Audio Tape, 30 min), and a sample of it has King preaching on adding the breadth of life to its length.

The King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 540228-001, titled "Rediscovering Lost Values," Sermon delivered at Second Baptist Church (Detroit), 2/28/1954 (Audio Tape), and samples of it have King on forgetting God in the pursuit of bank accounts and cars, and on segregation as blasphemy.

The King Institute's own mp3 server had no audio file for any known delivery of this sermon (17 May 1956, 24 Jul 1955 or 8 Jan 1956), and web searches turned up only transcripts and third-party readings, with no authorised recording.

OKRA lists the 4 Nov 1956 Dexter sermon only as paper documents (561104-000, 7 pp.; 561104-004, 10 pp.), not as an audio tape, and the King Institute's mp3 server had no file for the 1956 or 1958 deliveries; no authorised free recording was found.

The King Institute's own King Papers page for "The Birth of a New Nation," Sermon Delivered at Dexter Avenue Baptist Church (2021 archived version) links this exact file as "Listen to Audio"; it matches OKRA record 570407-003, and a sample of it has King describing Ghana's independence day with seventy nations represented.

rows.listen_label: King Institute (Stanford) recording – full service tape
rows.evidence: The King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 571117-002, titled "Loving Your Enemies," Sermon delivered at Dexter Avenue Baptist Church, [11/17/1957] (Audio Tape, 41.7 min); the file is a full service tape of about 2 hours, and the sermon in its first part includes King's "begin with yourself" point and the Abraham Lincoln story.

rows.listen_label: King Institute (Stanford) recording – Cincinnati, 11 Jun 1967 delivery
rows.evidence: OKRA holds the 11 Feb 1962 West Hunter tape (620211-000) but it is not online, so this links a later delivery: the King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 670611-001, titled "A Knock at Midnight," Sermon delivered at Mt. Zion Baptist Church, [6/11/1967] (Audio Tape), and a sample of it has King on the bread of faith and the bread of hope.

The King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 620916-000, titled "Levels of Love," Sermon delivered at Ebenezer Baptist Church, 9/16/1962 (Audio Tape, 36.5 min), and samples of it have King explaining eros as romantic love and asking what the highest good is.

This is a Strength to Love chapter (1963) that is still in copyright; the King Institute's mp3 server had no audio file for the 3 Apr 1960 Ebenezer sermon, and no authorised free recording or public-domain reading was found.

The King Institute mp3 (about 7 min) is named after OKRA record 630918-009, titled Expressions for Carol Denise McNair, Addie Mae Collins, and Cynthia Dionne Wesley delivered at Sixth Avenue Baptist Church, [9/18/1963] (Audio Tape, 7.0 min), and the audio includes the line that these girls died between the sacred walls of the church of God.

rows.listen_label: King Institute (Stanford) recording – sermon starts at about 14:10
rows.evidence: The King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 670827-000, titled "Why Jesus Called a Man a Fool," Sermon delivered at Mount Pisgah Missionary Baptist Church, [8/27/1967] (Audio Tape, 24 min); the file opens with a 1968 address by Coretta Scott King, and at about 14:10 the sermon is announced by name and King begins the parable of the rich fool from Luke.

The King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 680204-000, titled "The Drum Major Instinct," Sermon delivered at Ebenezer Baptist Church (Audio Tape); the audio opens with the Mark 10:35 reading about James and John and ends with King's "If I can help somebody as I pass along" close.

The existing Washington National Cathedral SoundCloud track is dead (SoundCloud oEmbed returns 404 and the wncathedral account is gone), so it is replaced by the King Institute mp3 named after OKRA record 680331-000, titled "Remaining Awake Through a Great Revolution," Sermon delivered at the National Cathedral (Audio Tape, 47 min); samples of it include the poverty passage and the Vietnam critique.

The King Institute mp3 is named after OKRA record 680403-001, titled I've Been to the Mountaintop, Address delivered at the Bishop Charles Mason Temple, and its ID3 tags read "Martin Luther King, Jr. Papers Project" with © 2006 MLKPP; the audio includes the injunction passage and the call to stand with the sanitation workers.
